chunks: The day the unbelievers are brought to the Fire, (it will be said): 'You wasted all your good deeds in the life of the world, and enjoyed them to the full. You will now be requited with a shameful punishment, for you behaved with arrogance for no reason on the earth, and acted wickedly.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reason for the humiliating punishment of disbelievers in the Hereafter according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the principle of *Jaza' al-Amal* (recompense for deeds), where the 'good things' (*tayyibat*) squandered in worldly life are not merely lost but serve as the basis for a humiliating punishment (*'adhab al-hawn*) due to the disbelievers' arrogance (*istikbar*) and transgression (*fisq*). The contrast emphasizes that their enjoyment was fleeting and ungrateful, leading to a degradation of status in the Hereafter that mirrors their earthly pride. This scene underscores the divine justice where the very blessings misused become the cause of their abasement.
